pharm-resp:targets.q: Which drug class targets IgE directly?
pharm-resp:targets.e: Omalizumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds free IgE, preventing binding to FcεRI on mast cells.

pharm-resp:targets.q: Bronchoconstriction in asthma is mediated mainly by:
o: α₂ receptors on airway smooth muscle
pharm-resp:targets.e: Parasympathetic M₃ tone and mast-cell mediators (LTC₄/D₄, histamine) constrict airways.

pharm-resp:targets.q: A 55-year-old man with mild asthma is started on propranolol for essential tremor. Two days later he presents with cough, chest tightness and diffuse expiratory wheeze. The mechanism of his bronchospasm is:
o: Direct agonism of M₃ receptors on airway smooth muscle
Blockade of β₂-mediated airway smooth muscle relaxation
IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation by the drug
Increased leukotriene synthesis from COX inhibition
pharm-resp:targets.e: Nonselective β-blockers remove β₂–cAMP bronchodilator tone, leaving M₃ and mediator constriction unopposed; leukotriene shunting is the mechanism of aspirin-exacerbated disease, not β-blockade.

pharm-resp:beta2.e: Salmeterol and formoterol are LABAs; albuterol is a SABA.

pharm-resp:beta2.q: LABA monotherapy in asthma is avoided because:
pharm-resp:beta2.e: LABA alone increases risk of severe exacerbation and death; LABAs are always combined with an ICS in asthma.

pharm-resp:beta2.q: A 16-year-old girl with asthma uses albuterol many times over a day during a cold. She notes fine hand tremor and palpitations; HR 118/min, serum K⁺ 3.1 mEq/L, creatinine normal. The low potassium is best explained by:
o: Aldosterone release driven by β₁ stimulation
Increased renal K⁺ loss via ENaC activation
β₂-stimulated Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase shifting K⁺ into cells
Gastrointestinal K⁺ loss from increased motility
pharm-resp:beta2.e: β₂ agonism activates Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase and drives K⁺ intracellularly (a transcellular shift); total-body K⁺ and renal handling are unchanged.

pharm-resp:steroids.q: Corticosteroids reduce airway inflammation chiefly by:
o: Blocking β₂ receptors in airway muscle
Blocking H₁ receptors on airway muscle
pharm-resp:steroids.e: Glucocorticoids suppress inflammatory gene transcription; first-line controller in chronic asthma.

pharm-resp:steroids.q: Which is a systemic effect of long-term oral steroids?
pharm-resp:steroids.e: Cushingoid effects: osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression, infection.

pharm-resp:steroids.q: A 45-year-old woman with severe asthma has needed prednisone 20 mg daily for 8 months. She now has sudden back pain; x-ray shows a T12 compression fracture and DEXA T-score is −2.8. The main mechanism of her bone loss is:
o: Excess vitamin D activation with hypercalciuria
Decreased osteoblast function and bone formation
pharm-resp:steroids.e: Glucocorticoids chiefly suppress osteoblasts (and reduce Ca²⁺ absorption), causing osteoporosis; they do not cause parathyroid hyperplasia.

pharm-resp:antimusc.e: Tiotropium is a long-acting M₃ antagonist used in COPD and asthma.

pharm-resp:antimusc.q: A typical adverse effect of inhaled antimuscarinics:
pharm-resp:antimusc.e: Anticholinergic effects: dry mouth; caution with glaucoma and urinary retention.

pharm-resp:antimusc.q: A 72-year-old man with COPD and benign prostatic hyperplasia starts a new once-daily inhaler for persistent dyspnea. One week later he has difficulty voiding and a palpable, distended bladder. Which drug was most likely started?
pharm-resp:antimusc.e: Tiotropium is an inhaled antimuscarinic (LAMA) that can precipitate urinary retention in BPH; salmeterol causes tremor and tachycardia, not retention.

pharm-resp:lt.e: Zileuton blocks 5-LOX; montelukast/zafirlukast block CysLT1 receptors.
Aspirin-induced asthma involves shunting to leukotrienes; neuropsychiatric effects are a boxed warning.

pharm-resp:lt.q: A 38-year-old woman with asthma and recurrent nasal polyps develops wheeze, rhinorrhea and facial flushing within an hour of taking ibuprofen for a headache. An oral add-on controller is chosen for her condition. Its mechanism is:
o: Stabilizes mast cells to block degranulation
Antagonizes H₁ receptors on airway muscle
pharm-resp:lt.e: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease shunts arachidonic acid to leukotrienes, so montelukast (CysLT1 antagonist) is useful; PDE4 inhibition is roflumilast for COPD.

pharm-resp:biologics.e: Anti-IL-5 for eosinophilic asthma; benralizumab targets the IL-5 receptor.
Used for eosinophilic asthma, atopic dermatitis and nasal polyps.

pharm-resp:biologics.q: A 50-year-old woman has severe asthma with 3 exacerbations in the past year despite high-dose ICS–LABA and good technique. Blood eosinophils are 650/µL and total IgE is normal. Which biologic best targets the main driver of her disease?
pharm-resp:biologics.e: Eosinophilic asthma responds to anti-IL-5 (mepolizumab); omalizumab targets IgE in allergic asthma with raised IgE.

pharm-resp:pde.q: Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic index; toxicity causes:
pharm-resp:pde.e: Methylxanthine; metabolized by CYP1A2, so CYP inhibitors raise levels.

o: Acute severe asthma in the ED
pharm-resp:pde.e: PDE4 inhibitor ↑cAMP in inflammatory cells; reduces COPD exacerbations.

pharm-resp:pde.q: A 66-year-old man with severe COPD and chronic productive cough (FEV₁ 40%) has 2 exacerbations a year despite LAMA + LABA. An oral drug is added that raises cAMP in inflammatory cells and reduces exacerbations. Which adverse effects are most expected?
pharm-resp:pde.e: Roflumilast (PDE4 inhibitor) commonly causes GI upset and weight loss; thrush and hoarseness come from inhaled corticosteroids.

pharm-resp:antihist.q: First-generation H₁ antihistamines differ from second-generation by:
o: Lower lipophilicity and less CNS entry
pharm-resp:antihist.e: They also have anticholinergic effects. Diphenhydramine and chlorpheniramine sedate; loratadine and fexofenadine do not.
Adverse effects: hypertension, CNS stimulation; rebound congestion with topical agents.

pharm-resp:antihist.q: A 78-year-old man takes an over-the-counter sleep aid at the labeled dose. The next morning he is confused, with dry mouth, dilated pupils and urinary retention. The drug's effects are best explained by:
pharm-resp:antihist.e: First-generation H₁ antihistamines such as diphenhydramine are lipophilic and anticholinergic, a Beers-list hazard in the elderly; they have no clinically relevant H₂ effect.

o: NMDA antagonism in the cough center
pharm-resp:cough.e: Acts centrally in the medulla; little analgesic or addictive potential; serotonin syndrome with SSRIs.

pharm-resp:cough.q: N-acetylcysteine as a mucolytic works by:
pharm-resp:cough.e: Thiol cleaves disulfide bonds; guaifenesin is an expectorant.

pharm-resp:cough.q: A 34-year-old woman taking sertraline uses an OTC cough syrup at the labeled dose for a cold. Two days later she is agitated and diaphoretic with temperature 38.6 °C, tremor, hyperreflexia and inducible clonus. Which cough-syrup ingredient is most likely responsible?
pharm-resp:cough.e: Dextromethorphan inhibits serotonin reuptake and can cause serotonin syndrome with SSRIs; guaifenesin is an expectorant without serotonergic action.

pharm-resp:pah.e: ↑cGMP causes pulmonary vasodilation. Prostacyclin analogs (epoprostenol) and riociguat are other options.

pharm-resp:pah.q: A 32-year-old woman has exertional dyspnea and a loud P₂. Right heart catheterization shows mean PA pressure 42 mm Hg, wedge pressure 10 mm Hg and a negative vasoreactivity test. She starts an oral drug that requires monthly liver tests and pregnancy tests. Its mechanism is:
pharm-resp:pah.e: Bosentan (endothelin receptor antagonist) is hepatotoxic and teratogenic; PDE5 inhibitors such as sildenafil need no routine LFT or pregnancy monitoring.

pharm-resp:delivery.q: A spacer with an MDI mainly:
o: Increases the dose needed per puff
Is designed for use with DPIs
pharm-resp:delivery.e: Less thrush and better lung delivery, especially in children.

o: A spacer attached to the mouthpiece
pharm-resp:delivery.e: Breath-actuated; poor in patients with low inspiratory flow.

pharm-resp:delivery.q: A 67-year-old woman with very severe COPD (FEV₁ 30%) and low peak inspiratory flow remains symptomatic on a dry powder inhaler despite a correct technique demonstration. She cannot inhale forcefully. Best next step:
o: Switch to an MDI with a spacer
Add an oral short-acting β₂ agonist
Increase the DPI dose to twice daily
pharm-resp:delivery.e: DPIs need fast, forceful inspiratory flow to disperse the powder; an MDI with spacer (or nebulizer) suits low-flow patients.

pharm-resp:cromolyn.e: Prevents mast cell degranulation; prophylactic only, not useful in an acute attack.
Very safe but must be used before exposure.

pharm-resp:cromolyn.q: A 10-year-old boy develops cough and wheeze 10 minutes into soccer practice. He is prescribed an inhaled agent to use 15 minutes before exercise; it has no bronchodilator effect and does not help once symptoms start. This agent works because it:
o: Antagonizes CysLT1 receptors on airway muscle
Activates β₂ receptors to raise airway cAMP
Binds free IgE, preventing FcεRI binding
pharm-resp:cromolyn.e: Cromolyn is a prophylactic mast cell stabilizer; β₂ agonists would bronchodilate and relieve active symptoms.

pharm-resp:cftr.e: Ivacaftor increases channel open probability in gating mutations (G551D); lumacaftor/tezacaftor/elexacaftor are correctors.

pharm-resp:cftr.q: Elexacaftor–tezacaftor–ivacaftor helps patients with at least one copy of:
pharm-resp:cftr.e: Triple therapy targets the most common folding mutation.

pharm-resp:cftr.q: A 14-year-old boy with cystic fibrosis has sweat chloride 98 mmol/L. Genotyping shows G551D on both alleles; the CFTR protein reaches the cell surface but rarely opens. Which drug best targets his defect?
pharm-resp:cftr.e: G551D is a gating mutation, so a potentiator that increases open probability is effective; correctors help folding defects such as F508del.

pharm-resp:chronicasthma.q: Preferred step-1/2 approach in adolescents and adults (GINA):
pharm-resp:chronicasthma.e: SABA-only treatment is no longer recommended.

pharm-resp:chronicasthma.q: Before stepping up therapy, first check:
pharm-resp:chronicasthma.e: Poor technique and adherence are the commonest reasons for poor control.

pharm-resp:chronicasthma.q: A 28-year-old woman with asthma uses albuterol about 4 days a week and wakes with cough once a week. She takes no controller; spirometry shows FEV₁ 85% predicted with 15% reversibility. Best next step in management:
pharm-resp:chronicasthma.e: Persistent symptoms need an ICS-containing controller (low-dose ICS–formoterol per GINA); LABA without ICS increases asthma deaths.

pharm-resp:acuteasthma.q: A sign of impending respiratory failure in acute asthma:
o: Rising PaCO₂ and a silent chest
pharm-resp:acuteasthma.e: A normal or rising CO₂ in a tachypneic patient suggests fatigue.

pharm-resp:acuteasthma.q: IV magnesium sulfate may be used in:
pharm-resp:acuteasthma.e: Given when severe exacerbations do not respond to initial therapy; Mg²⁺ relaxes bronchial smooth muscle.

pharm-resp:acuteasthma.q: A 22-year-old man in the ED with an asthma attack has received 1 hour of nebulized albuterol plus ipratropium and IV methylprednisolone. He is alert but still speaks in single words; peak flow is 30% of predicted, PaCO₂ 38 mm Hg. Best next therapy:
pharm-resp:acuteasthma.e: IV magnesium is the recommended add-on for severe exacerbations refractory to initial therapy; aminophylline adds toxicity with little benefit.

pharm-resp:stablecopd.q: Initial maintenance bronchodilator for most symptomatic COPD:
pharm-resp:stablecopd.e: Long-acting bronchodilators are the mainstay; ICS added for frequent exacerbations with eosinophilia.

pharm-resp:stablecopd.q: Which intervention improves survival in COPD with chronic hypoxemia?
pharm-resp:stablecopd.e: Smoking cessation and LTOT (PaO₂ ≤ 55 mm Hg) reduce mortality.

pharm-resp:stablecopd.q: A 68-year-old ex-smoker with COPD on LAMA + LABA has had 2 exacerbations needing oral prednisone in the past year. Blood eosinophil count is 400/µL. Best next step in maintenance therapy:
pharm-resp:stablecopd.e: Frequent exacerbations with eosinophils ≥ 300/µL favor escalation to LAMA + LABA + ICS; chronic oral steroids are not recommended.

pharm-resp:copdexac.q: Antibiotics in COPD exacerbation are indicated with:
o: Any new cough without other symptoms
pharm-resp:copdexac.e: Anthonisen criteria; common organisms: H. influenzae, S. pneumoniae, M. catarrhalis.

pharm-resp:copdexac.q: A 70-year-old man with COPD presents with worse dyspnea and purulent sputum; SpO₂ 82%. He is given high-flow oxygen to SpO₂ 99% and becomes drowsy, with PaCO₂ rising from 52 to 75 mm Hg. The main mechanism is:
o: ↑V/Q mismatch from loss of hypoxic vasoconstriction
Direct depression of the medullary chemoreceptors
Increased CO₂ production from fever and sepsis
pharm-resp:copdexac.e: Excess O₂ releases hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction (worsening V/Q) and adds a Haldane effect; loss of hypoxic drive plays only a minor role. Target SpO₂ 88–92%.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: หอบกลางดึก

boss.case: A 19-year-old woman with asthma uses her albuterol inhaler 4–5 days a week and wakes at night with cough and wheeze twice a week. She arrives in the ED after a cold with severe dyspnea, speaking in short phrases; SpO₂ 90%, diffuse wheeze.

qs.e: Repeated SABA (often with ipratropium) is the first step in an acute exacerbation.

qs.q: Which systemic therapy reduces relapse after this exacerbation?
qs.e: Oral or IV steroids speed recovery and reduce relapse in moderate–severe attacks.

o: M₃ blockade → ↓IP₃ → less airway muscle contraction
β₂ agonism → ↑cAMP → airway smooth muscle relaxation
qs.e: β₂–Gs–adenylyl cyclase–cAMP–PKA relaxes bronchial smooth muscle.

qs.q: A common adverse effect to monitor with repeated albuterol:
qs.e: β₂ agonists shift K⁺ into cells and cause tremor and tachycardia.

qs.q: At discharge, the best controller for her uncontrolled persistent asthma:
qs.e: Inhaled corticosteroid is the core controller; LABA must never be used without ICS (↑ asthma deaths).

qs.q: A key local adverse effect of inhaled corticosteroids:
qs.e: Thrush and dysphonia; rinse mouth and use a spacer.

title.th: สูบบุหรี่ 40 ปี เหนื่อยง่าย

stem.th: ชาย 66 ปี สูบบุหรี่ 40 pack-year เหนื่อยเวลาเดินขึ้นบันได ไอมีเสมหะทุกเช้า
stem.en: A 66-year-old man with 40 pack-years is breathless climbing stairs, with a daily morning productive cough.

steps.e: Long-acting bronchodilators are the mainstay of COPD.

info.th: Spirometry: FEV₁/FVC 0.58 หลังพ่นยาขยายหลอดลม

steps.e: ICS benefits COPD patients with frequent exacerbations and eosinophilia.

info.th: 2 ปีต่อมา กำเริบบ่อย eosinophil 400/µL
info.en: Two years later: frequent exacerbations, eosinophils 400/µL

steps.q: Roflumilast could also be considered because it:
o: Is a fast-acting bronchodilator for acute attacks
Blocks IL-5 and depletes blood eosinophils
steps.e: Used in severe COPD with chronic bronchitis and frequent exacerbations. Adverse effects: diarrhea, weight loss.
